# Component applicability map

<!-- Generated by `node compliance/src/cli.ts applicability --write` from compliance/applicability/rules.json. Do not edit by hand; `applicability --check` fails on any difference. -->

This page says, for each component the product and hosted levels assess, which controls it implements, supports or has no part in, and why. It is derived by rules from the component catalogue (`compliance/applicability/rules.json`): each component carries facets, short facts about what it is, each with the catalogue entry or code it rests on, and each control names the facets that give a component a part in it.

Your organization reviews this map. A component's cell reads "Not applicable to this component" with its reason only at a level whose review in `compliance/applicability/reviews.json` lists the component with the section SHA-256 shown below. When a section changes, its cells read Not met until your organization signs it again. A row no component has a part in reads "Your organization's responsibility", never Not applicable. The map says what each component is; it does not say that any control is met, and the decision to authorize a deployment remains your organization's.

The families that are wholly your organization's (AT, CA, MA, MP, PE, PM, PS, PT), the Classified appliance and the overlays are not part of this map.

## Facets

| Facet | A component that... |
|---|---|
| `access-decisions` | decides who may read or do what |
| `accounts` | keeps accounts for people or services |
| `admin-separation` | separates administration from ordinary use |
| `audit-records` | writes audit records of its own events |
| `audit-store` | stores, protects or reviews audit records |
| `authenticators` | issues, holds or checks authenticators (keys, tokens, certificates, passkeys) |
| `backup-restore` | keeps state that must be backed up and restored |
| `boundary-traffic` | controls traffic that crosses a network or air-gap boundary |
| `certificate-issuing` | issues certificates |
| `change-path` | is the path by which changes reach the system |
| `crypto-module-login` | is a cryptographic module that needs an operator login |
| `cryptography` | uses or manages cryptographic keys |
| `development` | is developed or rebuilt here, so the development process covers it |
| `device-identity` | identifies devices or nodes |
| `external-service` | is, or reaches, a service outside your organization |
| `federation` | accepts sign-ins from another identity provider |
| `hardware` | is hardware, or carries hardware into a site |
| `host-hardening` | runs on hosts whose kernel settings it controls |
| `identity-proofing` | registers people after their identity is checked |
| `integrity-checks` | detects unauthorized software or changes automatically |
| `labels` | reads or enforces security labels on information |
| `malicious-code-checks` | scans or refuses software for malicious content |
| `monitoring` | detects and reports security events |
| `name-resolution` | resolves names inside the site |
| `network-traffic` | sends or receives information over a network |
| `organization-data` | stores your organization's information at rest |
| `our-code` | is code this repository writes or rebuilds |
| `outside-users` | admits people from outside your organization |
| `pki-trust` | validates certificates or keys against a trust store |
| `privileged-remote` | takes privileged commands over a remote connection |
| `process-isolation` | runs work in isolated processes or containers |
| `re-authentication` | asks a signed-in person to sign in again before an action |
| `remote-access` | is the entry point for remote access |
| `separation-of-duties` | splits duties between roles |
| `sessions` | keeps sign-in or connection sessions |
| `shared-resources` | shares memory, storage or nodes between people |
| `sign-in` | signs people in or admits them only after a sign-in |
| `sign-in-page` | is the page where people sign in |
| `software` | is software or firmware we ship or deploy |
| `software-installation` | controls which software may be installed or run |
| `supplier-process` | carries the supplier's own policies, procedures, plans and records |
| `time-source` | sets the clocks of the nodes |
| `traffic-limits` | limits request rates or resource use against overload |
| `two-person-control` | needs two people for an action |
| `unauthenticated-entry` | is reachable before sign-in |
| `user-interface` | shows a user interface or runs code in a browser or editor |

### cert-manager

cert-manager issuing site certificates from the site PKI.

Levels: hosted-protected-a, hosted-protected-b. Section SHA-256: `4f1927e14fbc3be9a7643931d9947b6f6f5bce9e50e6d2bb0252f26fa9d998d6`.

Facets:

- `authenticators` (supports): resources.json image:quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-controller: the certificates it issues are the services' TLS authenticators.
- `certificate-issuing` (implements): resources.json image:quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-controller: issues and renews every TLS certificate at the site from the site's own CA.
- `cryptography` (implements): resources.json image:quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-controller: generates and renews certificate keys.
- `network-traffic` (supports): resources.json image:quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-cainjector: writes CA bundles so services can trust each other on the network.
- `pki-trust` (implements): resources.json image:quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-cainjector: writes the CA bundles the Kubernetes API trusts.
- `software` (implements): components/cert-manager.json: cert-manager is software every site runs.

### extension

The locally installed VS Code extension.

Levels: unclassified, protected-a, protected-b. Section SHA-256: `93521f0f442ca35c1b0a6bc71d845bfc0a528adc3e2a920da663d390b1566fc4`.

Facets:

- `access-decisions` (implements): src/domain/gate/decide.ts and src/gate/host.ts: the gate decides every tool, route and model request against the signed organization policy before it runs.
- `accounts` (supports): src/staff and src/domain/credentials: staff invitations, role changes and removals (G14) are recorded on the person's device; the accounts themselves are kept by your organization's identity provider and the hub.
- `admin-separation` (supports): src/domain/gate/layers.ts and src/gate/organizationStore.ts: the organization layer of the policy is signed by your organization's administrators and cannot be changed from an ordinary session.
- `audit-records` (implements): src/gate/decisionLog.ts: every gate decision is written to the local decision log (44.1-01 maps AU-02 to its tests).
- `audit-store` (implements): src/gate/decisionLog.ts: the local decision logs rotate at 5 MiB, keep four files and grant no group or other access (44.1-02-TRIAGE AU-04, AU-09).
- `authenticators` (implements): src/domain/did and src/gate/wallet.ts: the person's per-install Ed25519 identity key and the credentials in the wallet are held and checked on the device.
- `boundary-traffic` (implements): src/domain/gate/routing.ts and src/domain/gate/endpoints.ts: requests leave the device only to endpoints the signed policy allows (the route check).
- `cryptography` (implements): src/domain/credentials (ecdsaJcs2019.ts, dataIntegrity.ts) and src/domain/did/didKey.ts: signatures on policies, credentials and records; the crypto inventory lists its algorithms.
- `development` (supports): components/extension.json: the extension is this repository's code, built by the release pipeline (resources.json npm:typescript, npm:esbuild).
- `device-identity` (implements): src/gate/deviceIdentityCommand.ts and src/domain/did/deviceWords.ts: one Ed25519 identity per person per install, shown as six words.
- `external-service` (supports): src/domain/gate/endpoints.ts: the extension reaches the model endpoints your organization configures (the model-endpoints component).
- `labels` (implements): src/domain/gate/labels.ts, labelAlgebra.ts and src/gate/chatLabel.ts: classification labels on content and chats, and routing by label (Phase 70, CLAS-01 to CLAS-08).
- `malicious-code-checks` (supports): src/security/scan.ts and src/security/osv.ts: the extension checks a project's lockfiles against known-vulnerable package versions; the release pipeline scans the VSIX's own code (resources.json action:github/codeql-action/analyze).
- `monitoring` (supports): src/gate/decisionLog.ts: the gate records refused and allowed actions that your organization's monitoring can collect (G11 tracks forwarding).
- `network-traffic` (implements): components/extension.json and src/domain/gate/endpoints.ts: the extension sends prompts and context to model endpoints over TLS.
- `organization-data` (implements): src/gate/bundleStore.ts, src/gate/organizationStore.ts and the staff project store under src/staff: your organization's policy, projects and logs are kept on the device.
- `our-code` (implements): components/extension.json: the locally installed VS Code extension is written in this repository (src/).
- `pki-trust` (supports): src/domain/credentials/issuerAuthority.ts and src/domain/gate/trust.ts: issuer keys and trust anchors are checked before a credential or policy is accepted.
- `process-isolation` (supports): src/agent and src/mcp: agent tools and MCP servers run as separate processes that the gate starts and limits.
- `sign-in` (supports): src/domain/gate/enrolment.ts and src/domain/credentials/present.ts: enrolment and the person's credential presentation stand in for a sign-in to your organization's services.
- `software` (implements): components/extension.json: the extension is software shipped as the VSIX (resources.json lists its 41 packages).
- `software-installation` (supports): src/domain/gate/manifest.ts: tool and MCP server manifests decide which add-on software the agent may run.
- `user-interface` (implements): components/extension.json: the extension runs in VS Code and shows its chat and approval views there.

### hub

Optional synchronization hub.

Levels: unclassified, protected-a, protected-b, hosted-protected-a, hosted-protected-b. Section SHA-256: `43f496ad807004421aef291f6c91f9f4472db2e88aa0c59ee44e17e09ed3fc73`.

Facets:

- `access-decisions` (implements): hub/src/http/routes.ts and hub/src/append: the hub accepts an entry only from a member the project's roster allows.
- `accounts` (implements): hub/src/enrol.ts takes each project with its roster, hub/src/join.ts carries join requests for the lead's device to admit, and hub/src/store/schema.ts keeps each member's entries.
- `admin-separation` (supports): hub/src/enrol.ts: the operator's enrolment file is separate from members' sessions.
- `audit-records` (implements): hub/src/log/logger.ts and hub/src/log/redact.ts: the hub writes its own redacted log.
- `audit-store` (supports): hub/src/store/schema.ts: the hub keeps the signed append log of every project.
- `authenticators` (implements): hub/src/http/session.ts and hub/src/keys.ts: the hub checks members' signed session requests and holds its own signing key.
- `backup-restore` (implements): hub/src/checkpoints.ts and hub/src/stateDir.ts: the hub's state and signed checkpoints are backed up and restored (the local hub drill).
- `boundary-traffic` (supports): exchanges.json hub-sealed-bundles: sealed entries cross between hubs that are not connected.
- `cryptography` (implements): hub/src/keys.ts and hub/src/secrets.ts: the hub's signing key and the HMAC of enrolments.
- `development` (supports): components/hub.json: the hub is built in this repository (hub/) by the release pipeline.
- `device-identity` (implements): hub/src/join.ts and hub/src/enrol.ts: devices are admitted by their signed join requests.
- `labels` (implements): hub/src/store/schema.ts: each product stays in the cell for its label (Phase 32 Part B).
- `monitoring` (supports): hub/src/health.ts and hub/src/live/events.ts: health and live events for your organization's monitoring.
- `network-traffic` (implements): hub/src/http/server.ts: the hub is a network service over TLS.
- `organization-data` (implements): hub/src/store: shared staff projects of your organization are stored at rest.
- `our-code` (implements): components/hub.json: the hub is written in this repository (hub/src).
- `outside-users` (supports): exchanges.json hub-sealed-bundles: another organization's hub may carry sealed entries.
- `pki-trust` (supports): hub/src/http/server.ts: TLS-bound sessions are checked against the site certificates.
- `process-isolation` (supports): resources.json image:gcr.io/distroless/nodejs26-debian13: the hub runs alone in a minimal non-root container.
- `remote-access` (supports): components/hub.json: members reach the hub remotely to synchronize.
- `separation-of-duties` (supports): hub/src/enrol.ts and hub/src/join.ts: the operator enrols, the lead admits; neither does both.
- `sessions` (supports): hub/src/http/session.ts and hub/src/live/presence.ts: TLS-bound sessions and presence.
- `shared-resources` (supports): hub/src/store/schema.ts: one hub serves many projects in one store, separated by project and cell.
- `sign-in` (implements): hub/src/http/session.ts: members open a signed session before any request.
- `software` (implements): components/hub.json: the hub image is software this repository ships.
- `traffic-limits` (supports): hub/src/limits.ts: request sizes and token buckets that run before any signature check.
- `two-person-control` (supports): hub/src/join.ts: joining needs the lead's device and the six words read aloud, not the hub alone.
- `unauthenticated-entry` (supports): hub/src/health.ts and hub/src/join.ts: the health and join routes answer before a session exists.

### keycloak

Keycloak for passkey sign-in, with its realm applier and its Postgres database.

Levels: hosted-protected-a, hosted-protected-b. Section SHA-256: `7143dca3adadc6904e169291bbe1f0236292a96873d2c055d33181e24a29d05f`.

Facets:

- `access-decisions` (supports): resources.json image:quay.io/keycloak/keycloak: Keycloak issues the role claims that oauth2-proxy and the services act on.
- `accounts` (implements): resources.json tool:postgresql: Keycloak's database holds the user records and passkey public credentials of the site.
- `admin-separation` (implements): resources.json image:docker.io/adorsys/keycloak-config-cli: the realm is applied as code; the administration realm is separate from people's sign-in.
- `audit-records` (implements): resources.json image:docker.io/opensearchproject/opensearch: Keycloak events are sent to the site log store.
- `authenticators` (implements): resources.json image:quay.io/keycloak/keycloak: passkeys and hardware security keys only, no passwords.
- `backup-restore` (supports): resources.json tool:postgresql: Keycloak's database must be backed up and restored with the site.
- `change-path` (supports): resources.json image:docker.io/adorsys/keycloak-config-cli: sign-in settings change only through the reviewed realm applied at install and update.
- `cryptography` (implements): resources.json image:quay.io/keycloak/keycloak: Keycloak signs tokens and checks passkey signatures.
- `development` (supports): resources.json image:docker.io/adorsys/keycloak-config-cli: the realm settings are developed and reviewed in this repository.
- `federation` (implements): exchanges.json hq-sign-in-broker: an edge site's Keycloak accepts sign-ins brokered from HQ's Keycloak.
- `identity-proofing` (supports): exchanges.json site-mail: an administrator registers a person by a passwordless link to their email; proofing the person is your organization's.
- `monitoring` (supports): resources.json image:docker.io/opensearchproject/opensearch: Keycloak events reach the site log store for monitoring.
- `network-traffic` (implements): resources.json image:quay.io/keycloak/keycloak: the sign-in service answers over TLS.
- `organization-data` (implements): resources.json tool:postgresql: user records of your organization's people at rest.
- `our-code` (supports): resources.json image:docker.io/adorsys/keycloak-config-cli: the realm configuration is this repository's code.
- `outside-users` (implements): exchanges.json hq-sign-in-broker and user-export: people from another site are admitted.
- `pki-trust` (supports): exchanges.json revocation-sources: smart card certificates are checked against an OCSP responder or CRL.
- `privileged-remote` (supports): resources.json image:quay.io/keycloak/keycloak: administrators change the realm remotely.
- `re-authentication` (implements): resources.json image:quay.io/keycloak/keycloak: step-up sign-in (acr and auth_time) before signing.
- `remote-access` (supports): resources.json image:quay.io/keycloak/keycloak: every remote session signs in through Keycloak.
- `separation-of-duties` (supports): resources.json image:docker.io/adorsys/keycloak-config-cli: realm roles split administration duties.
- `sessions` (implements): resources.json image:quay.io/keycloak/keycloak: sign-in sessions and their lifetimes.
- `sign-in` (implements): resources.json image:quay.io/keycloak/keycloak: signs people in at the site with passkeys or hardware security keys only.
- `sign-in-page` (implements): resources.json image:quay.io/keycloak/keycloak: Keycloak serves the page where people sign in.
- `software` (implements): components/keycloak.json: Keycloak is software every site runs.
- `traffic-limits` (supports): deploy/keycloak/realm.json: brute-force detection limits sign-in attempts.
- `unauthenticated-entry` (implements): resources.json image:quay.io/keycloak/keycloak: the sign-in page is reachable before sign-in.
- `user-interface` (supports): resources.json image:quay.io/keycloak/keycloak: the sign-in and account pages run in the browser.

- `development` (supports): components/relay.json: the relay is built in this repository (relay/) by the release pipeline.

- `outside-users` (implements): components/relay.json: the relay admits senders from outside your organization (Phases 75 to 84).
- `pki-trust` (supports): relay/src/http/server.ts: TLS to the relay is checked against your organization's certificates.
- `process-isolation` (supports): resources.json image:gcr.io/distroless/nodejs26-debian13: the relay runs alone in a minimal non-root container.
- `remote-access` (supports): components/relay.json: outside parties reach your organization through the relay.
- `sessions` (supports): components/relay.json: the relay keeps sender connections (Phases 75 to 84).
- `sign-in` (implements): levels.json protected-b note: relay inbound authentication admits only signed-in senders.
- `software` (implements): components/relay.json: the relay image is software this repository ships.
- `traffic-limits` (implements): relay/src/http/server.ts: header count and slow-request time limits on every request.
- `unauthenticated-entry` (supports): relay/src/health.ts: the health route answers before any sign-in.

- `access-decisions` (implements): resources.json tool:rke2: Kubernetes RBAC decides what each workload and administrator may do.
- `accounts` (implements): resources.json tool:rke2: Kubernetes service accounts and role bindings for every site part.
- `admin-separation` (supports): resources.json tool:rke2: cluster administration runs through the Kubernetes API, separate from workloads.
- `audit-records` (implements): resources.json tool:rke2: RKE2 is installed with an audit policy (the Kubernetes audit log).
- `authenticators` (supports): resources.json tool:rke2: the API server checks client certificates and service account tokens.
- `backup-restore` (supports): resources.json tool:rke2: the cluster's etcd snapshots restore the site (47-27 recovery order).
- `boundary-traffic` (implements): components/rke2.json: Canal networking and network policies decide traffic between pods and out of the cluster.
- `certificate-issuing` (supports): resources.json tool:rke2: RKE2 issues the cluster's internal component certificates; site certificates are cert-manager's.
- `change-path` (supports): resources.json tool:helm: every site part is installed and updated on the cluster through helm.
- `cryptography` (implements): components/rke2.json: RKE2 in its FIPS build, with secrets encryption.
- `device-identity` (supports): resources.json tool:rke2: each node joins with its own node identity.
- `host-hardening` (supports): components/rke2.json: the CIS profile sets the node kernel settings.

- `name-resolution` (supports): resources.json tool:rke2: CoreDNS resolves names inside the cluster.
- `network-traffic` (implements): components/rke2.json: Canal networking carries every pod's traffic.
- `organization-data` (implements): resources.json tool:rke2: etcd holds the site's Kubernetes objects and secrets at rest (secrets encryption).
- `pki-trust` (supports): resources.json tool:rke2: the API server trusts its own cluster CA.
- `privileged-remote` (supports): resources.json tool:rke2: administrators reach the Kubernetes API remotely for privileged commands.
- `process-isolation` (implements): components/rke2.json: Kubernetes runs each workload in its own container and namespace.
- `remote-access` (supports): resources.json tool:rke2: the Kubernetes API is the remote entry point for administration.
- `separation-of-duties` (supports): resources.json tool:rke2: RBAC roles split cluster duties.
- `shared-resources` (implements): components/rke2.json: nodes are shared between many people's sessions.
- `sign-in` (supports): resources.json tool:rke2: administrators sign in to the API server.
- `software` (implements): components/rke2.json: RKE2 is software every site runs.
- `software-installation` (supports): resources.json tool:helm and image-registry: only the signed images the registry admits are run.
- `time-source` (implements): exchanges.json time-source: the site time source sets the cluster nodes' clocks.
- `traffic-limits` (implements): resources.json tool:rke2: resource quotas and limits on every workload.

### workbench

The Sterling workbench image that a hosted site runs for each person.

Levels: hosted-protected-a, hosted-protected-b. Section SHA-256: `dfeae8924fcdb93e9c0a07d294dade284b9590dd9a5089b35c138aaaa13752c0`.

Facets:

- `access-decisions` (implements): components/workbench.json and workbench/extension/src/node/egress-contribution.ts: the workbench reuses the extension's gate and allows egress only to policy-listed servers.
- `accounts` (supports): workbench/extension/src/common/session-identity.ts: the session runs as the signed-in person; the account itself is Keycloak's.
- `admin-separation` (implements): workbench/extension/src/common/key-service.ts: signing needs the step-up role (sterling-workbench-stepup) that an ordinary session does not hold.
- `audit-records` (implements): workbench/extension/src/browser/session-activity-frontend-module.ts and the extension gate log inside the image record the session's own events.
- `authenticators` (supports): workbench/extension/src/common/secret-store.ts and key-service.ts: the person's secrets and keys sit at their own OpenBao path, never in the image.
- `boundary-traffic` (implements): workbench/extension/src/node/egress-contribution.ts and exchanges.json model-servers and open-vsx: the session reaches only policy-listed model servers and the site extension mirror.
- `cryptography` (implements): workbench/extension/src/common/key-service.ts: signing through OpenBao's transit keys; TLS to OpenBao and the model servers.
- `development` (supports): components/workbench.json: the Sterling workbench image is built in this repository (workbench/Dockerfile) by the release pipeline.
- `device-identity` (supports): workbench/extension/src/common/identity.ts: the session is bound to the person's identity rather than a device; the node identity is RKE2's.
- `external-service` (supports): exchanges.json model-servers: workbench sessions send prompts to the model servers your organization's signed policy lists.
- `host-hardening` (supports): workbench/Dockerfile: the image runs as a non-root user on UBI 9 minimal; the node kernel settings are RKE2's.
- `labels` (implements): workbench reuses the extension's label handling (src/domain/gate/labels.ts) inside the image; 48.1-19 states ac-16 on it.
- `malicious-code-checks` (supports): resources.json tool:grype: the Release workflow scans the workbench image SBOM for known vulnerabilities before publishing.
- `monitoring` (supports): workbench/extension/src/browser/session-activity-frontend-module.ts: the session reports activity that the site's monitoring and Theia Cloud read.
- `network-traffic` (implements): exchanges.json model-servers and open-vsx: the session sends and receives over the network, over TLS.
- `organization-data` (implements): workbench/extension/src/browser/sterling-work-areas-module.ts and site-storage volumes: each person's workspace holds your organization's files.
- `our-code` (implements): components/workbench.json: the workbench extension and image are written in this repository (workbench/).
- `pki-trust` (supports): workbench/extension/src/node/backend-service.ts: TLS to OpenBao and the model servers is checked against the site CA.
- `process-isolation` (supports): components/theia-cloud.json: each person gets their own workbench container, which Theia Cloud starts and RKE2 isolates.
- `re-authentication` (supports): workbench/extension/src/common/key-service.ts: signing checks acr and auth_time and sends the person to step up first.
- `sessions` (supports): workbench/extension/src/common/session-identity.ts and session-activity.ts: the session view, its activity tracker and its retry.
- `shared-resources` (supports): components/workbench.json: many people's workbench containers share the site nodes and storage that RKE2 and site-storage separate.
- `sign-in` (supports): workbench/extension/src/browser/session-identity-frontend-module.ts: the session admits only the person oauth2-proxy signed in.
- `software` (implements): components/workbench.json: the Sterling workbench image is software a hosted site runs.
- `software-installation` (implements): exchanges.json open-vsx: the workbench installs extensions only from the site Open VSX mirror.
- `user-interface` (implements): components/workbench.json: the workbench is the browser editor each person uses.
